full_judgment: 12. Now comes the point of Stridhan. Petitioner as defendant No.4 entered appearance in the suit by filing written statement wherein she categorically stated that the suit schedule land is the stridhan Property belonging to Charubala. Defendant No.1 also admitted in his written statement that Charubala was the original owner of the suit land by purchase. D.W.I in his deposition categorically said that the suit schedule property is the Stridhan property of Charubala. Plaintiff did not controvert the statement that the suit schedule land is the Stridhan property of Charubala in any manner, either in writing or oral evidence. As such the contention that the suit schedule land is the "Stridhan Property" of Charubala remains un-controverted and thus admitted. In reversing the findings of the trial Court that the suit land is the "Stridhan property" of, Chantbala, the lower appellate Court took the recourse of presumption by holding that it is presume that at the time of purchase of the Suit land Charubala was residing in her husband's house which led Further presumption of the lower appellate Court that Charubala purchased the suit land with the monetary help of her husband. Such presumption without any evidence, written or oral, adduced by the plaintiff-appellant-opposite party No.1 or in absence of any statement in the plaint or without any suggestion at the time of deposition has no legal basis and not sustainable in law.
